detail.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61359. With `truncate_prompt_tokens` and an explicit `truncation_side`, truncation now keeps
the special tokens the tokenizer adds (`[CLS]`/`[SEP]`, BOS, EOS), as the tokenizer's own truncation
does. Before, the ones at the truncated end were cut.

## Claims

- Text prompts truncated from an explicit side keep their special tokens and match the tokenizer's
  own truncation on both sides, in `HfRenderer` and `MistralRenderer`: left truncation on BGE keeps
  `[CLS]`, right truncation on Qwen3-Embedding keeps the EOS it pools on, left truncation on Llama,
  and on Mistral in the `mistral` tokenizer mode, keeps BOS.
- Embeddings for these requests match `transformers` again: `LLM.embed`, `/v1/embeddings`, and
  Cohere `/v2/embed` with `truncate="START"`.
- `prompt_token_offsets` stay aligned with the kept tokens.
- Unchanged: requests without an explicit `truncation_side` (the tokenizer still truncates those
  itself), prompts without special tokens (`add_special_tokens=False`, the chat default), multimodal
  prompts, and the other renderers (see Details).

## Validation

`BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` on an RTX 3060 Laptop GPU (fp16, eager, V1 model runner as this machine has
no C compiler for Triton), `truncate_prompt_tokens=16`, three sentences longer than that. Cosine
similarity between vLLM's embeddings and the `transformers` model's (fp32) on the
`transformers`-truncated tokens, the same for `LLM.embed`, `/v1/embeddings` and Cohere `/v2/embed`:

| truncation | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| side unset (Cohere `truncate="END"`) | 1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000 | 1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000 |
| `"left"` (Cohere `truncate="START"`) | 0.9978, 0.9995, 0.9971 | 1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000 |
| `"right"` | 0.9890, 0.9700, 0.9917 | 1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000 |

On main, the prompt token ids from `LLM.embed` lack `[CLS]` (left) or the final `[SEP]` (right);
with this PR they match `transformers` for every prompt and side.

Render server (`vllm launch render hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM`, CPU),
`/v1/completions/render` with `truncate_prompt_tokens=4`:

| `truncation_side` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| unset | `[1, 17366, 11203, 29889]` | `[1, 17366, 11203, 29889]` |
| `"left"` | `[278, 17366, 11203, 29889]` | `[1, 17366, 11203, 29889]` |
| `"right"` | `[1, 450, 4996, 17354]` | `[1, 450, 4996, 17354]` |

`mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3` through `MistralRenderer` with `MistralTokenizer` (what
`--tokenizer-mode mistral` uses), tokenizer side `"left"` as for generate models,
`truncate_prompt_tokens=4`:

| `truncation_side` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| unset | `[1, 18666, 4682, 29491]` | `[1, 18666, 4682, 29491]` |
| `"left"` | `[1040, 18666, 4682, 29491]` | `[1, 18666, 4682, 29491]` |
| `"right"` | `[1, 1183, 3704, 9828]` | `[1, 1183, 3704, 9828]` |

Tokens from vLLM's renderer against `transformers` (`truncation=True, max_length=8`, same side):

| model | `"right"`, main → PR | `"left"`, main → PR |
|---|---|---|
| `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` | `[SEP]` dropped → match | `[CLS]` dropped → match |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` | `<\|endoftext\|>` dropped → match | match → match |
| `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` | match → match | BOS dropped → match |

The GPU and render-server numbers are from the previous revision of this PR. This one gives the
same token ids: I checked them again on CPU against `transformers` for these three models, both
sides, `max_length` 1, 2, 3 and 8, offsets included.

Tests, run on CPU (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`):

```bash
pytest tests/renderers/test_completions.py -k keeps_special_tokens  # 2 passed (both fail on main)
pytest tests/renderers/test_mistral.py -k keeps_bos                # 2 passed ("left" fails on main)
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py           # 45 passed (updated test fails on main)
pytest tests/renderers/test_completions.py tests/renderers/test_token_offsets.py \
  tests/renderers/test_truncate_after_mm_expansion.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_io_processor.py              # 179 passed
```

Both runs that include `test_render.py` also have 1 error,
`test_tokenize_matches_chat_render_for_gpt_oss`, whose model isn't in my offline cache.

I also ran `tests/renderers` with and without this change (main's four renderer files swapped in).
With it, 44 tests fail and 169 error, all for models not in my offline cache and the optional
`cohere_melody` package. `test_multimodal_hashes.py` and `test_process_multi_modal_uuids.py` can't
be collected offline, so I left them out. Without the change, the same tests fail, plus the new
ones: both `keeps_special_tokens` cases and the `"left"` case of `keeps_bos`. `pre-commit`
passes on the changed files.

Not a duplicate: I searched open and closed PRs and issues for `truncation_side` and for special
tokens lost on truncation. Related merged work (#43260, #47007, #54364, #54407, #54509, #54539,
#54692, #57076, #47772) adds the side, bounds tokenization, or keeps other fields aligned; none keeps
the special tokens. #58423 asks for message-aware chat truncation, which is a different problem.

## Details

Root cause: the tokenizer can only truncate from its own `truncation_side`, so with an explicit side
`get_encode_kwargs()` turns tokenizer truncation off and `_token_truncation` slices the full token
ids from the requested side. The slice doesn't know which tokens the tokenizer added and cuts the
ones at that end.

- `HfRenderer._tokenize_prompt`, for a prompt truncated from an explicit side, asks the tokenizer
  for `special_tokens_mask` in the same call and applies the indices that `get_truncation_indices`
  keeps to the token ids and offsets. `MistralRenderer._tokenize_prompt` does the same for BOS, the
  only token mistral-common adds, as `MistralTokenizer` can't return the mask.
  `apply_post_tokenization` then finds the prompt within the limit.
- `get_truncation_indices`, in `vllm/renderers/inputs/tokenize.py`, keeps the tokens that the mask flags and fits the text into
  the rest of the limit from the requested side, as `transformers` does. It returns `None`, so the
  plain slice applies, when no tokens were added or there is no room for them.
- `BaseRenderer` is unchanged, as asked in review. Each renderer handles what its
  own tokenizer adds, and no prompt is tokenized twice. The Cohere, Inkling and Kimi-K3 renderers
  have HF tokenizers but subclass `BaseRenderer`, so they still cut these tokens; they can take the
  same override in a follow-up. Multimodal prompts are skipped, since `_truncate_expanded_prompt`
  slices them again after placeholder expansion.

`test_completion_render_truncated_token_offsets` asserted that the first offset after left truncation
starts past the beginning of the prompt, which only held because BOS was dropped. It now checks that
BOS is kept with a `(0, 0)` offset.

When the special tokens alone exceed the limit (`truncate_prompt_tokens=1` with `[CLS] … [SEP]`), the
plain slice still applies instead of raising as `transformers` does.

Left out: cross-encoder pairs in `scoring/io_processor.py`, which slice the same way but also carry a
`[SEP]` between the segments and `token_type_ids`, and the Rust frontend's `PromptTruncation::apply`.

I used an AI assistant to investigate this and to write the code and tests; I reviewed every change
and ran the tests myself.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

inline_comments.body:
🟡 (optional) Long prompts truncated from an explicit side now cost twice the tokenizer CPU on the renderer's single default worker thread. The second call at base.py:701-704 re-tokenizes the whole pre-trimmed text, not a short one. That text is bounded only by `max_input_tokens * max_chars_per_token` characters, not by `truncate_prompt_tokens`. Fix: find the added tokens without a second full pass, e.g. `return_special_tokens_mask=True` on the first HF call, or a short probe string. Keep the re-tokenization only as a fallback for tokenizers that cannot report the mask, such as `MistralTokenizer`.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is any text request with `truncate_prompt_tokens` and an explicit `truncation_side` whose prompt is longer than the limit. In this mode `get_encode_kwargs` (params.py:382-386) turns tokenizer truncation off. The text is only pre-trimmed by `_text_len_check` (params.py:400-419) to `max_input_tokens * tokenizer.max_chars_per_token` characters, where `max_chars_per_token` is the longest vocab entry (hf.py:124). `_tokenize_prompt` (base.py:698-707) then tokenizes all of it a second time with `add_special_tokens=False`, just to learn which few tokens at either end were added. Tokenization runs in `self._executor`, which has `renderer_num_workers` threads and defaults to 1 (config/model.py:412). So every such request doubles its tokenizer time, and other requests queue behind it. On the base branch each prompt is tokenized once.

**Verification:** In this mode, `get_encode_kwargs` (params.py:382-386) returns `dict(truncation=False, add_special_tokens=...)`, so the first call at base.py:693 tokenizes all of the pre-trimmed text. The call at base.py:701-704 uses the same `truncation=False` kwargs, so it is a second full pass over the same text, not a short probe.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:nit -->

> @hmellor I am starting to hate how complicated this tokenization logic has become. Are there helper functions from Transformers that we could apply directly instead of this mess? I think most of this complexity is coming from the `truncation_side` argument.
> 
> cc @noooop

and `paddding` argument

For context on the Transformers side: there is no per-call `truncation_side`. In 5.19, `__call__` takes `padding_side` but not `truncation_side`, and the fast tokenizer reads `self.truncation_side` and writes it into the Rust tokenizer with `enable_truncation(direction=...)`. Setting it per request means changing state the tokenizer shares with every other request, so the renderer turns tokenizer truncation off and slices the ids itself. This PR only keeps the special tokens in that slice.

If Transformers took `truncation_side` per call the way it takes `padding_side`, the explicit-side path could use the tokenizer's own truncation, and both the slicing and the mask handling here would go away.

Thanks, good catch. Cohere, Inkling and Kimi-K3 have HF tokenizers but their own renderers, so they never asked for the mask either. I've dropped the mask and gone with your suggestion: when a prompt is truncated from an explicit side, the renderer tokenizes the text again with `add_special_tokens=False` and keeps the tokens around it. That works with any tokenizer, and `hf.py` is no longer touched.

Your example now gives `[1, 18666, 4682, 29491]` for `"left"`, and `test_explicit_truncation_side_keeps_bos` in `tests/renderers/test_mistral.py` covers both sides. The second tokenization only runs for prompts that an explicit side actually truncates.

Verified independently on CPU: the new tests fail on main and pass here; `tests/renderers` + pooling IO-processor unit tests: 118 passed; render-server offset tests pass. I also diffed against `AutoTokenizer(truncation_side=side)(…, truncation=True, max_length=k, return_offsets_mapping=True)` for bge-small-en-v1.5, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and tiny-random-Llama on both sides (k=3/8, incl. text containing a literal `[CLS]` and non-ASCII): ids and offsets match in every case. With a synthetic `[CLS] $A [SEP]` / `<s> $A` tokenizer all 8 tokenizer-side × requested-side combinations match HF (main gets 6/8 wrong).

@vadiklyutiy the rework in 7c6ee3218 follows your suggestion: the renderer now tokenizes the text again without special tokens instead of asking for the mask, so Mistral, and the Cohere, Inkling and Kimi-K3 renderers, keep BOS too. Could you take another look when you have a chance?

> I am starting to hate how complicated this tokenization logic has become. Are there helper functions from Transformers that we could apply directly instead of this mess? I think most of this complexity is coming from the `truncation_side` argument.

Sorry for the slow reply. Currently there is no helper on the Transformers side. If it's important we could make a feature request, but it may be de-prioritised until Tokenizers v1 is released.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

@hmellor I am starting to hate how complicated this tokenization logic has become. Are there helper functions from Transformers that we could apply directly instead of this mess? I think most of this complexity is coming from the `truncation_side` argument.

cc @noooop

The mask is only enabled in `HfRenderer` (`_can_produce_special_tokens_mask`), but the slice that drops the tokens is in the shared `BaseRenderer`, so other renderers still lose BOS with an explicit `truncation_side`.

E.g. `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3` with `--tokenizer-mode mistral`, `truncate_prompt_tokens=4`: side unset gives `[1, 18666, 4682, 29491]`, `"left"` gives `[1040, 18666, 4682, 29491]`. `MistralTokenizer` doesn't support `return_special_tokens_mask`, so this needs a fallback, e.g. re-tokenizing with `add_special_tokens=False` to find the added tokens.

**Nothing blocking.** The comments below are optional suggestions. There is no need to push a fix for them before merging.
